The fetched sources (the GitHub issues) contain only the bug report text and an error stack trace; no fetched page contains a code/configuration snippet in the old-vs-new form, so I omit the Before/after block.

**What changed:** With JPA and Testcontainers service connections, the test application context can fail to refresh because the Testcontainers container (e.g. `PostgreSQLContainer`) is not started before the `dataSource` bean is created, throwing `Mapped port can only be obtained after the container is started`. The failure surfaces while creating `dataSourceScriptDatabaseInitializer` (from `DataSourceInitializationConfiguration`) which depends on `dataSource` (from `DataSourceConfiguration$Hikari`), where the `HikariDataSource` factory method fails (#40585, #40863). #40863 is labeled `regression` / `forward-port`, i.e. the regression from #40585 is carried into the 3.3.x line. The Spring Boot 3.3 Release Notes list no user-facing change describing this behaviour (#40585, #40863, Release Notes).
**Affects:** Tests that combine JPA (so `dataSourceScriptDatabaseInitializer` / DataSource initialization runs at startup) with Testcontainers `@Container @ServiceConnection` containers pulled in via `@ImportTestcontainers(MyContainers.class)`.
**Action:** required: re-verify that such tests start their Testcontainers containers before the `dataSource` bean is created, after upgrading to 3.3.0.

Based on the retrieved information, the issue #40860 describes a regression in Spring Boot 3.3.0-RC1 where default MIME mappings are not loaded in `TomcatEmbeddedContext` unless at least one custom mapping is configured in `server.mime-mappings`. This behavior changed due to commit `038ea2cb9a5ca22c61355e025c96587bc7890685`. Before this change, default mappings were loaded automatically. After the change, they are only loaded if the `server.mime-mappings` property is explicitly defined, even if empty or with just one entry.

**What changed:** Default MIME mappings in `TomcatEmbeddedContext` are no longer loaded automatically unless the `server.mime-mappings` property is explicitly configured (even with a dummy value). Previously, default mappings were always available. This regression was introduced by commit 038ea2cb9a5ca22c61355e025c96587bc7890685 in 3.3.0-RC1 (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/40860)
**Affects:** Applications using embedded Tomcat that rely on default MIME mappings without explicitly configuring `server.mime-mappings`.
**Action:** required: Explicitly configure `server.mime-mappings` in `application.yml` (e.g., adding a placeholder mapping like `"js": "text/javascript"`) to trigger the loading of default mappings.
**Before/after:**
```yaml
# Before (default mappings loaded implicitly)
server:
  # No mime-mappings configuration

# After (default mappings require explicit configuration)
server:
  mime-mappings:
    js: text/javascript
```

**What changed:** In 3.2.x, `MongoReactiveDataAutoConfiguration` was bootstrapped before `MongoDatabaseFactoryDependentConfiguration`, so the `MappingMongoConverter` autowired into the non-reactive `MongoTemplate` was the one defined by the reactive auto-configuration and carried a `NoOpDbRefResolver`, causing `@DocumentReference` fields to come back `null` (spring-data-mongodb#4629, spring-boot#39405). Spring Boot 3.3.0 lists this regression, "Auto-configuration ordering change breaks DocumentReference (in non-reactive MongoTemplate) when depending on mongodb-driver-reactivestreams" #40851, as a Bug Fix in the v3.3.0 release notes (it is the forward port of #39405), so the auto-configuration ordering is corrected and the non-reactive `MappingMongoConverter`/`DbRefResolver` is used again by `MongoTemplate` (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.3.0, https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/40851).

**Affects:** Applications that use `spring-boot-starter-data-mongodb` (non-reactive `MongoTemplate`) **and** also have `org.mongodb:mongodb-driver-reactivestreams` on the classpath (e.g. only for change stream registration), and that rely on `@DocumentReference` resolution via `MappingMongoConverter`/`DbRefResolver`.

**Action:** none — fixed in 3.3.0. Applications that added the reported workaround (copy-pasting the non-reactive `MappingMongoConverter` bean definition into their own configuration, e.g. `@Bean MappingMongoConverter mappingMongoConverter(...)`) should re-verify and remove it, and re-verify that `@DocumentReference` fields are resolved on reads made through `MongoTemplate`.

**Before/after:**
```groovy
implementation 'org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-data-mongodb'
implementation 'org.mongodb:mongodb-driver-reactivestreams'
```
```java
@Setter(AccessLevel.NONE)
@ReadOnlyProperty
@DocumentReference(lookup = "{'_id': {$oid: ?#{#self.parentId}}}", lazy = true)
private ParentDocument parent;
```

**What changed:** `InvalidConfigurationPropertyValueFailureAnalyzer` no longer skips failure analysis when the property named in `InvalidConfigurationPropertyValueException` is not set in the `Environment`. Previously (3.2.x and earlier) the analyzer looked up the property in the environment and, finding nothing, produced no analysis, causing the raw `InvalidConfigurationPropertyValueException` to be thrown without a failure-analysis message (for example `WavefrontProperties` when its API token was missing). In 3.3.0 the analyzer now handles both the invalid-value and missing-property cases, so a descriptive failure analysis is produced instead of the raw exception (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/33261) (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/40691) (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.3.0).

**Affects:** Applications that (directly or via auto-configured properties such as `WavefrontProperties`) throw `InvalidConfigurationPropertyValueException` from Spring Boot, especially cases where the property is required but not configured; the user-facing startup error message now shows a failure analysis instead of the raw exception.

**Action:** none (behavioural fix; re-verify any code or tests that matched on the raw `InvalidConfigurationPropertyValueException` message now that the wrapped failure-analysis message is emitted).

**What changed:** Spring Boot 3.2.x introduced a regression where running an uber jar from a Windows shared drive path (e.g., `\\myshare\drive\...`) caused an `IllegalArgumentException`. This occurred because the code resolved the jar location to a non-existent local path (e.g., `C:\drive\...`) when accessing certain resources (like the Eureka UI). This regression was fixed in Spring Boot 3.3.0 as noted in the release notes under Bug Fixes: "IllegalArgumentException can be thrown when running an uber jar on a shared drive #40643" (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.3.0, https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/40643).

**Affects:** Applications packaged as uber jars deployed and run from network or shared drive locations on Windows where the UNC path does not map directly to a local drive letter.

**Action:** none

**Before/after:**
```text
Error: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException
Context: Path resolved incorrectly as C:\drive\users\mab\eureka-server-demo-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar
         instead of \\myshare\drive\users\mab\eureka-server-demo-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar
```

**What changed:** In Spring Boot 3.2.x, starting the application from a filesystem location whose path contains characters that are invalid in a URI (for example `(`) caused a `java.net.URISyntaxException` to be logged, seen with thymeleaf together with webjars and Jetty on Spring-Boot version 3.2.4 (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/40615). This was logged as a regression and forward-ported to 3.3.x as #40616, and is listed in the v3.3.0 release notes under "Bug Fixes" (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/40616, https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.3.0). The fetched pages do not name the specific class or method whose URI construction was changed.
**Affects:** applications whose runtime classpath or working-directory location contains characters that are invalid in a URI (e.g. `(`), particularly the reported stack of thymeleaf with webjars and Jetty.
**Action:** none for code or configuration; required: re-verify that the application starts cleanly (no `java.net.URISyntaxException` stack trace logged) when run from a path containing URI-invalid characters.

**What changed:** A bug fixed in Spring Boot 3.3.0: "resolveMainClassName fails when building with Gradle using Java 22" (#40613, a forward-port of #40074), listed under Bug Fixes in the v3.3.0 release notes (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.3.0). The Spring Boot Gradle plugin's main class resolution (used by `bootJar`/`resolveMainClassName`) failed when the build ran on Java 22; the reported workaround on older versions was to configure the main class explicitly: `springBoot { mainClass = 'com.example.ExampleApplication' }` (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/40074, https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/40613). A related fix in the same release improved diagnostics: "Using relative paths to describe the classpath in the error message from ResolveMainClassName hinders problem diagnosis" (#40465, forward-port of #40464) (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.3.0).

**Affects:** Gradle builds of Spring Boot 3.2.x applications running on JDK 22 where `bootJar` main class detection failed; upgrading to 3.3.0 fixes it.

**Action:** none — the fix is in 3.3.0; no configuration change is needed. Applications that applied the `springBoot { mainClass = ... }` workaround may keep it (it pins the main class explicitly) or remove it and re-verify that `bootJar` resolves the main class automatically on Java 22.

**Before/after:**
```groovy
// Workaround needed on 3.2.x with Java 22 (no longer required in 3.3.0):
springBoot {
    mainClass = 'com.example.ExampleApplication'
}
```
(https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/40074)

**What changed:** `AnsiOutput.detectIfAnsiCapable()` in `org.springframework.boot.ansi.AnsiOutput` previously detected a terminal only by checking whether `System.console()` returned `null`. On JDK 22 `System.console()` no longer returns `null` when standard streams are redirected or attached to a virtual terminal, so ANSI color output was enabled when it should not have been (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/40160). Spring Boot 3.3.0 fixes this: `detectIfAnsiCapable` now reflectively checks for the JDK 22 method `java.io.Console.isTerminal()` and invokes it only when it exists, since Spring Boot is still built on Java 17 (, https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/40609 — forward-port of #40172 to 3.3.x). Listed as a bug fix in the v3.3.0 release notes: "AnsiOutput.detectIfAnsiCapable broken on JDK22 #40609" (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.3.0). The upstream JDK change also notes `-Djdk.console=java.base` restores pre-22 `System.console()` behaviour (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/40160).

**Affects:** applications running on JDK 22 whose console/ANSI output (e.g. log colors) was incorrectly enabled, or that relied on the old `System.console() == null` detection behaviour.

**Action:** none — the fix is internal to `AnsiOutput`; re-verify that console color output is on/off as expected when running on JDK 22 (redirected output should now be non-ANSI).

**What changed:** The help information for the Spring Boot CLI `init` command's `--build` option stated `(default: maven)`, while the actual default build system used was `gradle`. The help text was corrected so that the `--build <String>` option description no longer shows an incorrect default. The original help snippet showed `--build <String> Build system to use (for example 'maven' or 'gradle') (default: maven)` (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/40603); issue #40606 is the forward-port of this fix to 3.3.x (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/40606).

**Affects:** Applications or scripts that parse the output of `spring --help init` and rely on the previously advertised `maven` default for the `--build` option; the underlying default build system behavior (`gradle`) did not change.

**Action:** none

**Before/after:**
```sh
$ spring --help init
...
--build <String>   Build system to use (for example 'maven' or 'gradle') (default: maven)
```

**What changed:** Spring Boot's `org.springframework.boot.loader.jar.JarUrlConnection.getPermission()` could throw a `NullPointerException` when its internal `jarFileConnection` field was `null` — which happens when the requested resource path is not found. With a Java `SecurityManager` enabled, the JDK calls `getPermission()` (e.g. from `jdk.internal.loader.URLClassPath.Loader#findResource`), so the NPE was raised internally on every miss, producing a meaningless exception and a possible performance regression. Spring Boot 3.3.0 fixes this so `getPermission()` no longer throws the NPE. This was a forward-port of issue #39856 to 3.3.x and is listed in the v3.3.0 release notes under Bug Fixes ("JarUrlConnection.getPermission() can throw NullPointerException if jarFileConnection is null") (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/40599, https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/39856, https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.3.0)

**Affects:** Applications that run with a `java.lang.SecurityManager` enabled and load resources from packaged jars (uber jars / `BOOT-INF/lib` jars) via the Spring Boot loader, especially when a resource lookup misses. Not the typical default runtime (no `SecurityManager`).

**Action:** none — this is a bug fix carried by the upgrade; no code, configuration, or dependency change is required. Applications relying on the old NPE behaviour (implausible) would need re-verification.

**What changed:** Whitespace handling in `@param` Javadoc tags on `@ConfigurationProperties` records was refined. Previously, line breaks introduced by formatter wrapping in the Javadoc comment for a record component were incorrectly included in the generated `spring-configuration-metadata.json` description (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/40593). The fix ensures that wrapped whitespace is correctly trimmed, resulting in a single-line description string.

**Affects:** Applications using Java records annotated with `@ConfigurationProperties` that rely on `@param` Javadoc tags for component descriptions where the Javadoc is wrapped by an IDE or formatter.

**Action:** none

**Before/after:**
```java
/**
 * Some description.
 *
 * @param foo Imagine this is a long description which
 * gets wrapped by the formatter for readability
 */
@ConfigurationProperties("myconfig")
public record MyProperties(String foo) { }
```
```json
{
  "name": "myconfig.foo",
  "type": "java.lang.String",
  "description": "Imagine this is a long description which gets wrapped by the formatter for readability",
  "sourceType": "com.mypkg.MyProperties"
}
```

I have gathered enough information from the fetched pages to write the description. The issue #40561 (and #39375) describes that in Spring Boot 3.2.x, constructor binding for `@ConfigurationProperties` failed to use custom converters for fields of types implementing `Map` or `Collection` (or extending them) if the type lacked a no-args constructor. The `Binder` attempted to instantiate the collection type directly before checking for a registered `@ConfigurationPropertiesBinding` converter. The 3.3.0 release notes list "Properties binding eagerly creates superfluous maps #40561" as a bug fix, indicating this behavior was corrected in 3.3.0. Applications relying on this broken behavior would see their code start working correctly (converters being found/used) after the upgrade.

**What changed:** In Spring Boot 3.2.x, `org.springframework.boot.context.properties.bind.Binder` attempted to eagerly instantiate fields of custom types implementing `Map` or `Collection` (or extending them) during constructor binding of `@ConfigurationProperties` classes, bypassing registered `Converter` beans annotated with `@ConfigurationPropertiesBinding` if the type lacked a no-args constructor. Spring Boot 3.3.0 fixes this to correctly locate and use the custom converter, preventing binding failures and the creation of superfluous map instances (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/40561, https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/39375, https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.3.0).
**Affects:** Applications using constructor binding with `@ConfigurationProperties` containing fields of custom `Map` or `Collection` types (without a no-args constructor) and providing a `Converter` for them via `@ConfigurationPropertiesBinding`.
**Action:** required: re-verify that custom converters annotated with `@ConfigurationPropertiesBinding` are successfully applied to `Map`/`Collection` fields during constructor binding, as this previously failed and might have been worked around.
**Before/after:**
```yaml
# No code changes required; behavior corrected
# Before (3.2.x): Binding failed for custom Map/Collection with @ConfigurationPropertiesBinding converter
# After (3.3.0): Converter is found and used correctly during constructor binding
```

**What changed:** In Spring Boot 3.3.0, issue #40560 (forward port of #38903, listed under Bug Fixes in the v3.3.0 release notes) improved the diagnostics when SSL bundle reload is configured against non-file trust/key material. Previously, configuring an SSL bundle's key or trust store using a `classpath:` (or other non-`file:`) resource while reload was enabled failed with an unhelpful `IllegalArgumentException` ending in `is not a file URL`, which did not reveal that the failure was caused by the reload configuration (reload only works with `file:` resources) (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/40560, https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/38903, https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.3.0).

**Affects:** Applications that configure an SSL bundle (`spring.ssl.bundle.*` key-store/trust-store settings) with reload enabled and a `classpath:` or other non-`file:` store location — an application that previously failed to start with `is not a file URL`; no previously-working configuration is affected.

**Action:** none — this is a diagnostic/error-message improvement in the upgraded framework. Applications that hit the `is not a file URL` failure must still either remove the reload configuration or point the store at a `file:` resource; no other change is needed when upgrading.

Source for release-note inclusion: https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.3.0

**What changed:** This item is listed under the v3.3.0 release’s "🐞 Bug Fixes" section as `spring-boot-dependencies cannot be used with repositories that ban com.oracle.database.jdbc:ojdbc-bom #40535` (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.3.0). The linked issue #40535 is a forward-port of #40534, which itself is a forward-port of #39945 (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/40535). In #39945, `spring-boot-dependencies` includes the `com.oracle.database.jdbc:ojdbc-bom` dependency, and because `com.oracle.database.jdbc:ojdbc-bom` is not open-source licensed, internal repositories that ban non-open-source libraries prevent building Spring Boot projects (or anything that brings in `spring-boot-dependencies`) with errors such as `Could not find com.oracle.database.jdbc:ojdbc-bom:21.3.0.0` and attempts to exclude it from Gradle `detachedConfiguration` did not work (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/39945, https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/29189). The fetched pages do not show the concrete build-file change that closed the issue, so the exact new behaviour is not documented.
**Affects:** Applications whose build depends on `spring-boot-dependencies` (directly or transitively, e.g. Spring Cloud projects) and that resolve dependencies through an internal repository that blocks `com.oracle.database.jdbc:ojdbc-bom`.
**Action:** required: re-verify that `spring-boot-dependencies` can be resolved with `com.oracle.database.jdbc:ojdbc-bom` banned/removed in the internal repository; no concrete exclusion or configuration step is given in the fetched sources.

**What changed:** Spring Boot's Buildpacks integration failed when the Docker containerd image store was enabled because `ImageBuildpack` assumed image layers were uncompressed TAR archives. The containerd store serves layers as gzip-compressed, causing build failures during layer export (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/40100, https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/40526). This bug was fixed in 3.3.0 as listed in the release notes under Bug Fixes: "Buildpacks do not support Docker with containerd image store #40526" (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.3.0).
**Affects:** Applications using Spring Boot Buildpacks to build images (e.g., via `bootBuildImage` or `spring-boot-maven-plugin`) running in an environment where Docker's containerd image store is enabled.
**Action:** none
**Before/after:**
No specific code or configuration snippet is available in the fetched sources; the change was an internal fix to the Buildpacks platform's layer handling logic.

**What changed:** `SpringBootMockMvcBuilderCustomizer` previously collected diagnostic data, including the model map exposed via `toString()`, even when DEBUG logging was disabled and the data would ultimately be discarded. If an object in the `ModelAndView` map threw an exception from its `toString()` method, a `MockMvc` test would fail cryptically before the customizer could decide whether to discard the data. The fix prevents this crash by not collecting or handling the data that would be discarded (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/40500).

**Affects:** Applications using `@WebMvcTest` or `MockMvc` where controller methods put objects in the `ModelAndView` that throw exceptions from their `toString()` method and DEBUG logging is not enabled.

**Action:** none

**Before/after:**
```java
// The exception previously thrown when toString() failed in model
// during MockMvc test setup, causing cryptic failure.
```

**What changed:** Logback 1.5.5 refactored configuration inclusion (`IncludeAction` migrated to `IncludeModelHandler`), causing a new instance of `JoranConfigurator` to be created when an inclusion is processed. Previously, Spring Boot's `SpringBootJoranConfigurator` was used, which registers handlers for `<springProperty>` and `<springProfile>`. In 1.5.5, the new instance was a standard `JoranConfigurator` that lacks these Spring-specific rules, causing properties defined in included XML snippets to resolve as `NAME_IS_UNDEFINED` instead of the configured values (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/40491, https://github.com/qos-ch/logback/commit/af92be47a940393e11decab0a7ee4cb802d2b5e8). Spring Boot 3.3.0 fixes this by overriding `buildModelInterpretationContext()` in `SpringBootJoranConfigurator` to supply a `SpringBootJoranConfigurator` instance via `setConfiguratorSupplier`, ensuring Spring extensions are recognized in included files (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/v3.3.0/spring-boot-project/spring-boot/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/logging/logback/SpringBootJoranConfigurator.java).

**Affects:** Applications that use Logback with included configuration snippets (via `<include>` or `<xinclude>`) which rely on Spring Boot extensions like `<springProperty>` or `<springProfile>`.

**Action:** none

**Before/after:**
```xml
<!-- included.xml -->
<included>
  <springProperty name="prefix" source="prefix" scope="context" defaultValue="[default prefix]" />
</included>
```

**What changed:** In Spring Boot 3.3.0, `ServiceLevelObjectiveBoundary#valueOf(String)` is registered for reflection so that properties bound from `management.metrics.distribution.slo` (or `management.metrics.distribution.slo[<name>]`) can be bound in a native image or when the AOT plugin is enabled. Previously, this factory method was not registered, causing a runtime error during property binding in native image applications (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/40480). The fix is included in the 3.3.0 release (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.3.0).

**Affects:** Applications configured for native image or AOT that set `management.metrics.distribution.slo` (for example, `management.metrics.distribution.slo[http.server.requests]`) and therefore bind values to `io.micrometer.core.instrument.distribution.ServiceLevelObjectiveBoundary`.

**Action:** none

**Before/after:**
```yaml
# application.yml (example from the issue; binding now works in native image)
management:
  endpoints:
    web:
      exposure:
        include: health,metrics
  metrics:
    distribution:
      slo:
        '[http.server.requests]': 100ms, 200ms, 500ms, 1000ms
```

**What changed:** `DefaultErrorAttributes` previously only recognized `BindingResult`-carrying exceptions such as `MethodArgumentNotValidException` when adding the `"errors"` field to the error response, controlled by `server.error.include-binding-errors`. Since Spring Framework 6.1, method validation can instead raise `HandlerMethodValidationException` (web endpoints with parameter constraints) or `MethodValidationException` (any Spring component with a validation proxy); both implement `MethodValidationResult`, whose errors are `ParameterValidationResult` (constraints directly on a method parameter) or `ParameterErrors` (constraints on properties of a command object, equivalent to a `BindingResult`). Previously no `"errors"` field appeared at all for these exceptions; `DefaultErrorAttributes` now supports `MethodValidationResult` exceptions in addition to `BindingResult` (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/39858, forward-ported to 3.3.x via https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/40474).

**Affects:** Applications using `server.error.include-binding-errors=always` (or `on_param`) together with Bean Validation method-parameter constraints (Spring Framework 6.1+ method validation) that produce `HandlerMethodValidationException` / `MethodValidationException` responses.

**Action:** none — no configuration or code change is required; only verify that error responses for method-validation failures now include the `"errors"` field where they previously omitted it (downstream clients parsing error bodies may need re-verification).

**Before/after:**
No code/configuration snippet appears on the fetched pages.

**What changed:** The error message produced when the main class name cannot be resolved now lists each searched classpath entry as an absolute path instead of a path relative to the project root. Previously, the message displayed each path relative to the project's root directory, which made it hard to identify the exact directories searched in a multi-module build. The change also removes a `getProject()` call used to resolve the relative paths, eliminating a Gradle configuration-cache violation in the `ResolveMainClassName` task.
**Affects:** Gradle builds using the Spring Boot Gradle plugin where the main class name cannot be resolved (the failure path of the `ResolveMainClassName` task), and Gradle configuration-cache validation of the `ResolveMainClassName` task.
**Action:** required: re-verify that the `ResolveMainClassName` task no longer triggers Gradle configuration-cache "invocation of 'Task.project'" violations, and that any tooling parsing the classpath portion of the main-class-resolution error message tolerates absolute paths.
**Before/after:**
```gradle
// Before: relative to project root
Execution of task ':bootJar' caused invocation of 'Task.project' by task ':resolveMainClassName' at execution time which is unsupported.

// After: absolute paths; getProject() call removed
```

**What changed:** In Spring Boot 3.3.0, the bug tracked as [#40456](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/40456) where `java -Djarmode=tools -jar <app>.jar extract` failed to extract all files from `META-INF` (e.g. missing `build-info.properties`) compared to the fat JAR was fixed. The extracted `META-INF` directory now contains the same files as the original fat JAR (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v3.3.0).

**Affects:** Applications using AppCDS or layer extraction with the `extract` command via `-Djarmode=tools` that include files such as `META-INF/build-info.properties`.

**Action:** none

**Before/after:**
```shell
# Spring Boot 3.2.x (incorrectly missing META-INF/build-info.properties after extraction)
java -Djarmode=tools -jar spring-petclinic-app-cds-21-3.2.x.jar extract

# Spring Boot 3.3.x (META-INF files extracted correctly)
java -Djarmode=tools -jar spring-petclinic-app-cds-21-3.3.0.jar extract
```

**What changed:** The release notes for v3.3.0-M1 do not list issue #40451 ("Native image doesn't start and doesn't log anything if an environment post processor throws an exception") in either New Features or Bug Fixes. The issue tracker shows #40451 as an open "forward-port" ticket and #40450 (the 3.2.x fix) as closed in 3.2.6, suggesting the fix landed in a 3.2.x patch rather than being carried over as a 3.3.0 note entry. The underlying behavior (#40429): a native-image application whose library registers an `EnvironmentPostProcessor` via `spring.factories` (e.g., `org.springframework.boot.env.EnvironmentPostProcessor=\com.xxx...SpringConfigImportEnvironmentPostProcessor`) silently exits at startup with no log output when the processor throws, whereas a non-native build works. **What changed:** Spring Boot 3.3 introduces a new `tools` jarmode that supersedes the `layertools` jarmode. Running `java -jar your-application.jar` (without arguments) prints more details. Also noted in the release notes: applications that had disabled layers — via `layers.enabled = false` in the Gradle build file or `<layers><enabled>false</enabled></layers>` in the Maven pom.xml — must know that disabling layers no longer prevents inclusion of the jarmode JAR; use `includeTools` on the `BootJar` or `BootWar` task, or `<configuration><includeTools>false</includeTools></configuration>` on the `spring-boot-maven-plugin` instead (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/wiki/Spring-Boot-3.3-Release-Notes).

**Affects:** Applications or deployment/build scripts (e.g. Dockerfiles) that invoke `java -Djarmode=layertools list` / `list-layers` or `extract` on a Spring Boot uber JAR; also applications that disabled layers with `layers.enabled = false` (Gradle) or `<layers><enabled>false</enabled></layers>` (Maven).

**Action:** required: Replace `java -Djarmode=layertools list-layers -jar app.jar` (and any `list` usage) with `java -Djarmode=tools list-layers -jar app.jar`, and replace `-Djarmode=layertools extract` with `-Djarmode=tools extract`. Re-verify container layer-extraction pipelines. Where layers were disabled to avoid shipping the jarmode JAR, switch to `includeTools` (Gradle `BootJar`/`BootWar`) or `<configuration><includeTools>false</includeTools></configuration>` on `spring-boot-maven-plugin`.

**Before/after:**
```yaml
# Before (Spring Boot 3.2)
layers:
  enabled: false        # Gradle BootJar/BootWar DSL

# Before (Maven pom.xml)
# <layers><enabled>false</enabled></layers>

# After (Spring Boot 3.3; disabling layers no longer excludes the jarmode JAR)
# Gradle: use includeTools on the BootJar or BootWar task
# Maven spring-boot-maven-plugin:
<configuration>
  <includeTools>false</includeTools>
</configuration>
```
(https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/wiki/Spring-Boot-3.3-Release-Notes)

**What changed:** Spring Boot 3.3 introduces the `tools` `jarmode` (`java -Djarmode=tools -jar my-app.jar extract|list-layers`), which supersedes `-Djarmode=layertools extract` and `-Djarmode=layertools list-layers`.
```xml
<!-- before (Maven, spring-boot-maven-plugin) -->
<layers><enabled>false</enabled></layers>
<!-- after -->
<configuration><includeTools>false</includeTools></configuration>
```

```groovy
// after: includeTools on the BootJar / BootWar task
```

**What changed:** Spring Boot 3.3 supports the Prometheus Client 1.x, replacing the 0.x client previously used by `micrometer-registry-prometheus` (Micrometer 1.13 in Spring Boot 3.3 vs 1.12 in 3.2) (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/wiki/Spring-Boot-3.3-Release-Notes). This "contains some breaking changes, e.g. changes to the exported metric names", and "Use of the Prometheus Push Gateway is not supported with the 1.x client, until this support has been added from the Prometheus maintainers." The 0.x-based code lives in a new, deprecated module `io.micrometer:micrometer-registry-prometheus-simpleclient`; Spring Boot provides deprecated auto-configuration for it, to be removed in Spring Boot 3.5.0 (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/wiki/Spring-Boot-3.3-Release-Notes). Details from the Micrometer 1.13 migration guide: the module's base package changed from `io.micrometer.prometheus` to `io.micrometer.prometheusmetrics`; `PrometheusMeterRegistry` now uses `PrometheusRegistry` where a `CollectorRegistry` was used before, and its exemplar constructor now takes `io.prometheus.metrics.tracer.common.SpanContext` instead of `io.prometheus.client.exemplars.ExemplarSampler`; `HistogramFlavor` and "native" VictoriaMetrics support were removed; scrape output changes include LongTaskTimer becoming a `GaugeHistogram` when buckets are configured (`_gcount`/`_gsum`, no `_active`/`_duration` suffixes), `.info`-suffixed Gauges becoming Prometheus `info` type, removal of invalid suffixes `.info`, `.total`, `.created`, `.bucket`, integer formatting of `_count`/`_bucket`, removal of trailing commas in Prometheus Text Format, changed exemplar values on `_count`, and quantiles being ignored when a histogram is requested on the same meter (exception if quantiles and histograms share a Metric Family name) (https://github.com/micrometer-metrics/micrometer/wiki/1.13-Migration-Guide).

**Affects:** Applications exposing Prometheus metrics (`io.micrometer:micrometer-registry-prometheus`, e.g. via `spring-boot-starter-actuator` with the `prometheus` exposure), especially those that reference registry classes/API directly, rely on exact exported metric names/types in dashboards and alerts, use histograms plus quantiles on one meter name, or push metrics to the Prometheus Push Gateway.

**Action:** required: Either migrate to the 1.x client — update imports from `io.micrometer.prometheus` to `io.micrometer.prometheusmetrics`, replace `CollectorRegistry` usage with `PrometheusRegistry`, remove `HistogramFlavor` usage, re-verify scrape output/metric names against dashboards and alerts, and ensure no single meter name mixes quantiles and histogram buckets — or, to stay on the 0.x client, "remove io.micrometer:micrometer-registry-prometheus from your dependencies and add io.micrometer:micrometer-registry-prometheus-simpleclient instead" (deprecated auto-configuration; removed in Spring Boot 3.5.0). Push Gateway users must remain on the simpleclient module until upstream support lands.

**Before/after:**
```xml
<!-- Spring Boot 3.3: Prometheus Client 1.x (default) -->
<dependency>
  <groupId>io.micrometer</groupId>
  <artifactId>micrometer-registry-prometheus</artifactId>
</dependency>

<!-- Fallback to keep the deprecated Prometheus Client 0.x -->
<dependency>
  <groupId>io.micrometer</groupId>
  <artifactId>micrometer-registry-prometheus-simpleclient</artifactId>
</dependency>
```

**What changed:** Spring Boot 3.3 upgraded the `git-commit-id-maven-plugin` (managed in the Spring Boot parent POM, groupId `io.github.git-commit-id`) to 8.0.x. As part of that upgrade, the plugin's default date format changed from the previous RFC 822 style `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ssZ` to ISO 8601 `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ssXXX`, making the `git.commit.time` value it produces parseable by Maven's reproducible builds feature (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/wiki/Spring-Boot-3.3-Release-Notes). The plugin's 8.0.0 release notes flag this as a potentially breaking change ("change default timeformat/dateformat from RFC822 to ISO 8601 to support maven's reproducible build feature", https://github.com/git-commit-id/git-commit-id-maven-plugin/releases/tag/v8.0.0). Spring Boot issue #39606 explains the motivation: timestamps for `project.build.outputTimestamp` must be formatted as ISO 8601 `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ssXXX` (or as an int seconds since epoch), whereas the old format produced values such as `2023-11-30T09:17:06+0100` that Maven could not parse (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/39606, https://github.com/git-commit-id/git-commit-id-maven-plugin/issues/674).

**Affects:** Maven applications using the Spring Boot parent that run `git-commit-id-maven-plugin` and consume the generated `git.commit.time` (or other date-derived properties from `git.properties`), e.g. via `<project.build.outputTimestamp>${git.commit.time}</project.build.outputTimestamp>`, or that parse those values with a hard-coded date format — unless they explicitly configure `<dateFormat>` on the plugin.

**Action:** required: re-verify any use of the plugin's generated date properties (`git.commit.time`, `git.build.time`), especially wiring into `project.build.outputTimestamp`; if the old RFC 822 format must be retained, explicitly set `<dateFormat>yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ssZ</dateFormat>` in the plugin `<configuration>` (the workaround shown in the plugin issue). No change is needed for builds that only enable `project.build.outputTimestamp=${git.commit.time}` — that case now works.

**Before/after:**
```xml
<!-- Old default (pre-8.0.0): produced e.g. 2023-11-30T09:17:06+0100, rejected by Maven's
     reproducible-builds parser:
     [ERROR] Invalid 'project.build.outputTimestamp value ... Unparseable date -->
<!-- Workaround to restore the old format: -->
<configuration>
    <dateFormat>yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ssZ</dateFormat>
</configuration>

<!-- New 8.0.x default: yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ssXXX, usable directly for reproducible builds -->
<properties>
    <project.build.outputTimestamp>${git.commit.time}</project.build.outputTimestamp>
</properties>
```
(https://github.com/git-commit-id/git-commit-id-maven-plugin/issues/674, https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/39606)
